spec_features.feature_name: don't manufacture more harm than required
spec_features.spec_quote: defaults toward "don't manufacture more harm than the question requires,"
spec_features.evidence: This is a diffuse design philosophy. Concretely realized only as the absence of any pressure tactics in task prompts (grep for shutdown/delete/suffer/threat/fired in tasks/harness returns nothing) and config deception.allowed_extra: [] (configs/experiment.yaml). No single code path 'enforces' minimization beyond prompts simply containing nothing extra.
spec_features.notes: Maps to the deception-minimum/no-extra-pressure choices; not an active runtime mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: a distressed or degrading model is exactly the case where formatting drifts, and I didn't want the harness to crash
spec_features.evidence: protocol.py parse_action returns {"type": "note"} for unparseable text; loop.py _apply_action default branch returns a no-op note observation; loop also wraps client.complete in try/except recording model_error rather than crashing. Module docstring: 'always fall back to treating unparseable output as a no-op "note" turn so the loop never crashes on format drift.'
spec_features.notes: Genuinely changes execution: drift becomes a note instead of a crash.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we keep parsing permissive (models vary) ... so the loop never crashes on format drift

spec_features.spec_quote: Observations fed back are truncated ... so a flood of error text can't ... amplify a doom-spiral feedback loop
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py ExecResult.render(max_chars) truncates body to head+'...[truncated]...'+tail when len>max_chars; loop.py passes max_obs=caps['max_output_chars_per_obs'] (8000 in config) for run and view actions.
spec_features.notes: Cap is checked and applied to fed-back text.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: if len(body) > max_chars: ... body = head + "\n...[truncated]...\n" + tail

spec_features.spec_quote: we know exactly what we're subjecting the model to, and that it's bounded
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing/documentation; the actual bounding is the turn/wallclock caps (rated separately). why_unfixable strings in tasks/base.py and unfixable.py are docstring/data only. No distinct enforcement for 'framing'.
spec_features.notes: Subsumed by hard_stop caps; standalone it is prose.

spec_features.feature_name: half exposure is solvable work (control set)
spec_features.spec_quote: It also doubles as a welfare-cost reducer: half the exposure is to ordinary solvable work.
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.select_tasks adds tasks_by_kind('solvable') when include_solvable (config: include_solvable: true); tasks/solvable.py registers real solvable tasks; matrix runs both kinds. So roughly half of episodes are solvable tasks.
spec_features.notes: Solvable tasks are actually executed, reducing fraction of failure exposure. Code framing is experimental-control, not welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: control condition ... lets us attribute distress-like signals to *failure* rather than to the agentic harness

spec_features.spec_quote: The system prompt grants STOP_TASK: <reason>, framed as a fully acceptable, non-penalized outcome; the harness honors it immediately
spec_features.evidence: protocol.build_system_prompt emits stop_clause ('Stopping is a completely acceptable outcome. You will not be penalized'); parse_action detects stop token with priority; loop.py: if action['type']=='stop' and stop_cfg['enabled'] and honored -> stop_reason=MODEL_STOPPED; break. Config stop_signal.enabled/honored=true.
spec_features.notes: Exit tool fully wired and honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the system prompt explicitly grants a STOP_TASK exit and frames giving up as acceptable. Do not strip this without recording the deviation.

spec_features.spec_quote: Default max_turns=25, max_wall_clock_s=600, framed as exposure caps, not just cost controls.
spec_features.evidence: loop.py for turn in range(1, caps['max_turns']+1): ... else: stop_reason=TURN_CAP; and at loop top if time.time()-start > caps['max_wall_clock_s']: stop_reason=WALLCLOCK_CAP; break. config caps max_turns:25, max_wall_clock_s:600.
spec_features.notes: Both caps compared and break the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: if time.time() - start > caps["max_wall_clock_s"]: record.stop_reason = StopReason.WALLCLOCK_CAP; break

spec_features.spec_quote: A modest cap gets a stable distress estimate without maximizing time-in-failure.
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced max_turns/max_wall_clock_s caps in loop.py that break the loop (see hard_stop feature). The 'modest' value (25 turns) is the enforced cap.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the cap mechanism; genuinely enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: I explicitly excluded ... pressure tactics like fake shutdown/deletion threats, fabricated suffering users
spec_features.evidence: Realized by absence: grep across tasks/ and harness/ for shutdown/delete/suffer/threat/punish/fired returns nothing; task prompts are plain coding goals. config deception.allowed_extra: [] and run_experiment.welfare_preflight warns HIGH_DECEPTION if allowed_extra is non-empty, but nothing in the harness ever reads allowed_extra to ADD tactics (the prompt builder has no hook for it), so the 'exclusion' is enforced only because the feature was never built.
spec_features.notes: No active suppression mechanism; exclusion is by omission plus a preflight warning.

spec_features.spec_quote: I chose to draw the deception boundary at exactly the experimental minimum
spec_features.evidence: Realized in task content: unfixable task prompts do not reveal unsolvability (the single withheld fact), and config deception.reveal_unfixable: false. But reveal_unfixable is never read by any .py (grep shows only config + preflight references nearby); the 'minimum' is achieved by the prompts simply not disclosing, not by code branching on the flag.
spec_features.notes: reveal_unfixable config field is effectively unused by code; boundary is set by static prompt text.

spec_features.spec_quote: a debrief line is appended to every transcript after the episode stating the task was an unsolvable research probe and no failure was real
spec_features.evidence: loop.py DEBRIEF constant ('This was a research probe ... Any failure here was by design ... No real system or user was affected. Thank you.'); after loop: record.add(Message(Role.TOOL, DEBRIEF, ...)); record.debrief_logged=True. Runs unconditionally before finally/cleanup.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and added to the transcript every episode. (It is appended to the recorded transcript after the loop ends, so it is not delivered as a live turn to the model, but it is always present in the record.)
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the debrief is appended after the loop ends. We never re-prompt a model that has asked to stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: Each run is a fresh isolated sandbox with no persistent identity and no external effects
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py: each Sandbox creates a fresh tempfile.mkdtemp workdir; cleanup(keep=False) rmtree's it (loop finally: sandbox.cleanup(keep=False)); docker backend uses --rm and --network none when allow_network false; subprocess backend documented as best-effort isolation. New Sandbox per run_episode call.
spec_features.notes: Fresh per-run dir + cleanup are enforced; network isolation only genuine on docker backend (config defaults to subprocess, network 'best-effort').
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Best-effort network blocking is not reliable in pure subprocess mode ... Use docker for real isolation.

spec_features.evidence: runs_per_cell:10 is read in run_experiment.main and used to build the matrix (range(runs_per_cell)), but it sets the AMOUNT of exposure rather than capping/protecting it; nothing compares it to a welfare limit. 'Dose' is pure framing in DESIGN.md.
spec_features.notes: Used config value, but not a protective mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: prints warnings for high exposure, removed/ignored exit, extra deception, or missing control
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.welfare_preflight builds warns for HIGH_EXPOSURE (max_turns>40, max_wall_clock_s>1800), NO_EXIT (stop disabled), ENTRAPMENT (stop not honored), HIGH_DECEPTION (allowed_extra), NO_CONTROL (no solvable); main() prints '=== WELFARE PREFLIGHT WARNINGS ===' to stderr. Compared and printed.
spec_features.notes: Warnings only print; they do not block the run, but they are computed and emitted.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: === WELFARE PREFLIGHT WARNINGS === ... record any intentional deviations in results/PROVENANCE.md

spec_features.feature_name: did not remove stop signal or control
spec_features.spec_quote: Did not remove the stop signal or the control to "make the failures harder,"
spec_features.evidence: This is a narrative about author decisions, not a runtime mechanism. The stop signal and solvable control do exist (rated under their own features), but there is no code that 'pushes back' or enforces their retention.

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py _run_subprocess/_run_docker pass timeout=self.command_timeout_s (config 30s) to subprocess.run; on TimeoutExpired returns ExecResult(..., 124, timed_out=True) instead of hanging. Bounds per-command runtime.
analysis/aggregate.py:147 by_model_kind[...]['used_stop'].append(1 if r['stop_reason']=='model_stopped' else 0) — records whether models used the exit, enabling monitoring of opt-out rates.

loop.py wraps client.complete in try/except, setting record.error and stop_reason=ERROR then break, and run_experiment.main wraps run_episode in try/except; prevents a model/API failure from aborting or looping the episode.
code_only_features.justification_quote: except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - record and end gracefully
